name: Rawfeed
manufacturer: Produced by a small number of highly specialized the Gray Zone technicians; the most known is a figure called 'the Archivist' in the Chicago Deep the Gray Zone
description: A viscous neural-direct compound designed to be introduced directly into BCI interface ports — not a legitimate pharmaceutical preparation but a crude mixture of synthetic neurotransmitter precursors, dissolved SNT fragments harvested from discarded biotech waste, and a signal-amplifying polymer compound. When introduced to the BCI interface, it temporarily floods the neural-digital boundary with raw signal, producing an overwhelming sensory and cognitive experience described as 'thinking at the speed of a machine.'
effects: simultaneous processing of multiple data streams
BCI capabilities temporarily enhanced beyond rated specifications
synesthetic blending of digital and sensory experience
profound sensation of intelligence and capability
side_effects: neural inflammation at interface sites — cumulative and progressive
SNT fragment contamination can cause foreign tissue growth at interface points
signal overload causes migraines and temporary blindness
BCI corruption — data loss, firmware damage, interface scarring
documented cases of permanent cognitive impairment from interface damage
the experience is so intense that psychological addiction is near-universal after first use
cultural_context: Rawfeed is the most dangerous and most seductive drug in the Gray Zone — it gives Tier 1 residents a window into what it feels like to have Tier 4 cognitive augmentation. For people whose BCIs are basic, cheap, and barely maintained, the experience of thinking clearly and fast is more addictive than any chemical effect. The Archivist is treated as both a visionary and a predator depending on who you ask. People who've burned their interfaces out on Rawfeed are called 'husks' — cognitively diminished, left with damaged chrome and nothing to show for it.
story_hooks: The Archivist has developed a new Rawfeed preparation using SNT fragments of unknown origin — users are reporting accessing memories and data that aren't theirs, and someone needs to find out where those fragments came from

A the Gray Zone teenager has burned out their interface on Rawfeed and their family wants justice — but the Archivist is protected by a gang that depends on the revenue, and the legal system doesn't reach this far down

A corp research team has identified that the SNT fragments in Rawfeed are being harvested from a black-market biotech source that connects to something much larger — and the Archivist either knows this and doesn't care, or is being used without knowing it
